# seedfall

> Deterministic simulation testing for Go. seedfall compiles your unmodified Go services for `wasip1`, runs a whole cluster on one simulated clock, and owns every source of nondeterminism: time, randomness, goroutine scheduling, disk and network. When an invariant breaks you get the seed, the exact fault schedule and a full trace, and `seedfall shrink` cuts the schedule down to the few faults that matter.

Install with `go install github.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/cmd/seedfall@latest`. `seedfall init` onboards a Go module, `seedfall mcp` serves every command to coding agents over MCP, and the skills below teach an agent the full loop. The complete text of every page is in [llms-full.txt](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/llms-full.txt).

## Docs

- [Using seedfall from AI coding agents](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/agents.md): `seedfall mcp` serves seedfall's core operations over the [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) on stdio. An agent such as Claude Code, Cursor or Codex can then sweep seeds, replay a failure and shrink it on its own, then use the exact fault schedule and trace to fix the bug and prove the fix. No API key and no hosted service are involved: the agent you already use does the reasoning.
- [Running Antithesis SDK code](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/antithesis.md): Code instrumented with the [Antithesis Go SDK](https://github.com/antithesishq/antithesis-sdk-go) runs under seedfall unchanged. Assertions become seedfall properties, `lifecycle.SetupComplete` becomes seedfall's setup signal, and `random.GetRandom` draws from the seed.
- [Causality analysis](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/cause.md): `seedfall shrink` tells you which faults are *needed* for a failure. `seedfall cause` tells you *when the failure became likely*, and which event made it so.
- [Running seedfall in CI](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/ci.md)
- [Storage engines that need mmap or flock](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/compat.md): Some storage libraries don't build or run for `GOOS=wasip1` because they call `mmap`, `flock` or other syscalls that WASI doesn't have. With `compat_overlay`, seedfall swaps their platform files for small `wasip1` versions at build time, so you test the library you ship, unmodified:
- [Configuration and faults](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/faults.md): A world is described in a JSON file, `seedfall.json` by default. Paths inside it are relative to the file.
- [Getting started](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/getting-started.md): This walkthrough uses `examples/kvlog`, a small log-structured key-value server, to find a real durability bug, shrink it, fix it and prove the fix. It takes about five minutes.
- [Use your Gostman collections as workloads](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/gostman.md): A [Gostman](https://github.com/kunalgoesbyken/gostman) collection already says what your API promises: each request carries checks such as `res.status equals 200` or `res.body equals {{value}}`. Gostman's Go `runner` package builds for `wasip1`, so a seedfall workload can load the collection and send it while seedfall crashes your service, tears its writes and partitions its network. A check that fails after the faults stop is a broken promise, reported with the request and the check, and replayable from its seed.
- [How seedfall works](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/how-it-works.md)
- [Inspecting the disk at the moment of failure](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/inspect.md): `seedfall replay` tells you what happened. `seedfall inspect` shows you what is on disk when it goes wrong: every file on every node, how much of it is durable, which bytes a crash would lose, which directory entries are not durable yet, and where the last crash tore a write.
- [Mutation testing your durability checks](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/mutate.md): A sweep that passes is only meaningful if your workload would notice when durability breaks. `seedfall mutate` tests that directly: it weakens the simulated disk under your nodes, one guarantee at a time, and checks whether your sweep catches it.
- [Networking](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/networking.md): seedfall gives every node a simulated network: ordered byte streams with seeded latency, partitions that hold traffic until they heal, and connection resets when a peer crashes. Node names are host names, so a node named `server` is reachable at `server:7000`.
- [Properties, linearizability and determinism](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/properties.md)
- [Triage reports](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/reports.md)
- [Testing seedfall itself](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/testing.md): seedfall is only useful if its own model of crashes, faults and replay is right, so that model has its own tests. This page lists what they check and how to run them.
- [Proving a fix with `seedfall verify`](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/docs/verify.md): `seedfall verify` is the definition of done for a change that fixes a seedfall failure, whether a person or an AI agent wrote it. It answers one question with evidence: is the failure gone, and how sure are we?

## Agent skills

- [seedfall-fix-and-prove](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/skills/seedfall-fix-and-prove/SKILL.md): Fix a triaged seedfall failure and prove the fix. Replays the saved minimal fault schedule until it passes, sweeps fresh seeds, then runs seedfall verify for a 95%-confidence proof with determinism and mutant checks, and puts the Markdown proof block into the pull request. Use after seedfall-triage, or whenever a change to storage, recovery or replication code must be shown crash-safe before it is merged.
- [seedfall-properties](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/skills/seedfall-properties/SKILL.md): Read a Go service's storage and replication code, turn its durability and consistency promises into seedfall properties (sim.Assert, sim.Always, sim.Sometimes, sim.Reachable, sim.Unreachable, and linearizability through sim.Put and sim.Get), and grade them with seedfall mutate until every exercised durability mutant is killed. Use after seedfall-setup, when asked what to check, to strengthen a workload, or when a green sweep might be proving nothing.
- [seedfall-setup](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/skills/seedfall-setup/SKILL.md): Set up seedfall deterministic simulation testing in a Go module that has no seedfall.json yet. Checks that the services build for wasip1, scaffolds seedfall.json and a workload with seedfall init, wires the workload to the service, and runs the first seed sweep. Use when asked to add seedfall, crash testing, deterministic simulation testing or fault injection to a Go service.
- [seedfall-triage](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/skills/seedfall-triage/SKILL.md): Triage a failing seedfall seed down to a root cause before touching code. Classifies the failure, shrinks the fault schedule, finds the fault that made the failure inevitable with seedfall cause, inspects the simulated disk at the failure, then checks the hypothesis with a counterfactual replay of an edited schedule. Use when seedfall run, the seedfall GitHub Action or a CI sweep reports FAIL seed N.

## Optional

- [README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/kunalgoesbyken/seedfall/main/README.md): bugs found, quickstart, features, examples and limitations
- [Findings](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/)
- [Open creates the database file without fsyncing its directory, so one crash can lose the whole database](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/bbolt-create-dir-fsync.html)
- [AutoRecovery fails on ordinary torn tails, so Open errors out after a crash mid-Put](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/bitcask-autorecovery-torn-tail.html)
- [Open rewrites config.json in place without fsync, so a crash can leave the database permanently unopenable](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/bitcask-config-json-torn.html)
- [AutoRecovery renames an unsynced copy over the last datafile, so a second crash can wipe acknowledged writes](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/bitcask-recovered-datafile-fsync.html)
- [Acknowledged writes can be lost after a datafile rotation (no directory fsync) or after a failed fsync (offset not rewound)](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/bitcask-rotation-dir-fsync-and-eio.html)
- [WriteStream with sync and TempDir doesn't fsync the directory after the rename, so an acknowledged write can revert after a crash](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/diskv-rename-dir-fsync.html)
- [FileSnapshotStore doesn't fsync the snapshot directory before rename, so a crash can leave an empty snapshot after logs were compacted](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/hashicorp-raft-snapshot-dir-fsync.html)
- [A crash in the middle of a log append makes the node unable to restart, now or after its next restart](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/jmsadair-raft-log-torn-tail.html)
- [Snapshots are ordered by wall-clock time, so after the clock steps back a restart loads an old snapshot and the node never starts again](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/jmsadair-raft-snapshot-wall-clock-order.html)
- [The term and vote file is renamed into place without an fsync, and one crash leaves a node that can never restart](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/jmsadair-raft-state-file-fsync.html)
- [A crash while a snapshot is being written leaves a temporary directory that makes every later start fail](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/jmsadair-raft-tmp-snapshot-dir.html)
- [A crash during stream creation leaves meta.inf without meta.sum, and the stream then disappears on every later restart](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/nats-stream-meta-checksum-crash.html)
- [`bucket.Meta` is never fsynced, so a crash can make recovery drop every entry in the bucket](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/nutsdb-bucket-meta-fsync.html)
- [Acknowledged writes can be lost after a data-file rotation (no directory fsync) or after a failed fsync (offset not rewound)](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/nutsdb-rotation-dir-fsync-and-eio.html)
- [A torn write at the end of the active data file makes Open fail with "crc error" on every restart](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/nutsdb-torn-tail-crc.html)
- [rosedblabs/wal appends after a torn chunk, so one crash mid-write makes later fsynced writes unreachable and rosedb can no longer open](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/rosedblabs-wal-torn-tail.html)
- [Shrink renames the rewritten AOF over the database without fsyncing it, so a crash after a shrink can wipe the database](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/tidwall-buntdb-shrink-fsync.html)
- [tidwall/wal can't reopen after a crash mid-append, and the pending fix (#22) leaves stale bytes that corrupt the log after the next segment rotation](https://seedfall-lemon.vercel.app/proof/tidwall-wal-torn-tail.html)
